claims.claim: The legacy XML feed at https://www.boi.org.il/currency.xml no longer serves XML. Verified 2026-08-27: it answers HTTP 301 with Location https://boi.org.il/PublicApi/GetExchangeRates, and the final response is JSON. Agents must not parse XML.

claims.claim: The live JSON endpoint returns an exchangeRates array whose objects each carry key, currentExchangeRate, currentChange, unit and lastUpdate.
currentChange is a percentage daily move (for example -0.47 for USD on 2026-08-26), not an absolute NIS delta, and it is not used in conversion math.

The Bank of Israel publishes a representative rate for exactly 14 currencies: USD, GBP, JPY, EUR, AUD, CAD, DKK, NOK, ZAR, SEK, CHF, JOD, LBP, EGP. Verified live on 2026-08-27: the endpoint returned exactly these 14 keys.

claims.verified_via: api (full response enumerated on 2026-08-27; the array contained exactly these 14 key values)

claims.claim: Units vary by currency: JPY unit = 100, LBP unit = 10, most others unit = 1. The SDMX series expresses the same basis as UNIT_MULT, where unit = 10 ** UNIT_MULT (USD 0, LBP 1, JPY 2).

The JSON endpoint's ?date= parameter is ignored: passing an old date still returns the most recently published rate with an unchanged lastUpdate. Verified live on 2026-08-27 against no-date, ?date=2025-06-03 and ?date=2026-01-01.

Historical rates come from the BOI SDMX EXR dataflow. Base path https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/ ; series pattern https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/BOI.STATISTICS/EXR/1.0/RER_<CUR>_ILS ; concrete example https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/BOI.STATISTICS/EXR/1.0/RER_USD_ILS . With startPeriod, endPeriod and format=csv the response is a CSV whose columns include TIME_PERIOD and OBS_VALUE; read on 2026-08-11 the first 2026 USD observation is 2026-01-02 at 3.181 and the last in the window is 2026-01-15 at 3.156. Covers these references: https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/BOI.STATISTICS/EXR/1.0/RER_USD_ILS?startPeriod=2026-01-01&endPeriod=2026-01-15&format=csv

claims.claim: The representative rate is published once per business day, and the JSON endpoint keeps returning the previous publication until the next one lands, so a call made before the day's publication returns the previous business day's rate. This is why the rate's date must be taken from lastUpdate and never from the system clock. Verified 2026-08-27 at 02:08 UTC: the endpoint returned lastUpdate 2026-08-26 while the SDMX series had no observation for 2026-08-27 yet. The Bank of Israel's explanatory notes give the clock times (about 15:15 on regular days, about 12:15 on Fridays and holiday eves) but that page is JS-rendered and returns a browser challenge to automated fetches, so the exact times are NOT machine-verifiable from this skill and must be treated as indicative; lastUpdate is the authority.
claims.verified_via: api (publication-lag behaviour verified against the endpoint and the SDMX series; the clock times themselves are not machine-verifiable and are flagged as indicative in the skill)

claims.claim: The Bank of Israel sets a single representative rate per currency, with no buy/sell spread: each object in the response carries exactly one currentExchangeRate.

For imports into Israel priced in foreign currency, the customs value on an import declaration (rashimon) uses the customs rate published weekly by the Israel Tax Authority, not the bare Bank of Israel representative rate. The Tax Authority's exchange-rate service returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches and could NOT be verified on 2026-08-27, so this skill instructs the reader to read the published customs rate rather than derive it, and flags the commonly-cited 0.5% uplift and the weekly effectivity window as unconfirmed. Imported services under reverse-charge VAT use the plain representative rate with no customs uplift.
claims.raw_snippet: UNVERIFIED: the Israel Tax Authority exchange-rate service returned HTTP 403 to an automated fetch on 2026-08-27, so no snippet could be quoted and the skill routes the reader to the published rate instead of asserting a derived figure.
claims.verified_via: UNVERIFIED (bot-blocked; the skill deliberately asserts no derived customs figure as a result)

claims.claim: Bank of Israel representative rates published 2026-08-26, used in this skill only as labelled illustrative examples: USD 2.972 NIS per 1 unit, and JPY 1.8684 NIS per 100 units (about 2.97 ₪ and about 1.87 ₪ respectively). The JSON endpoint returns the rate together with its own lastUpdate stamp, which is the publication date and is not necessarily today.

The Lebanese pound is published on a 10-unit basis (SDMX UNIT_MULT = 1) at an observation value so small that a per-unit rate rendered at four decimal places displays as 0.0000 ₪ even though the converted total is correct. The skill therefore widens the displayed precision instead of reporting a zero rate.

claims.claim: Israeli number formatting places the shekel sign before the amount and uses a comma as the thousands separator and a period as the decimal separator, so one thousand two hundred thirty four and fifty six agorot is written 1,234.56 ₪ and never 1.234,56 in the European convention. This is a presentation convention of the skill's own output, not an external regulatory fact, and the bundled script emits amounts in this form.
claims.verified_via: self-declared output convention (no external source is claimed; the rate object is cited only to anchor the worked amount)
